chapter_title: Concerning the Fifteen Paths; and whether the Catechumen would have avoided causing his Wealth to go on the Three Paths to Gehenna
chapter_note: Only a small core substrate survives here: a compact, systematic cosmological teaching on the fifteen paths in the “zone” and the three waste-paths to the gehennas (¶2–4, embedded inside a question-summary). The remainder is dominated by later institutional soteriology about elect/catechumens, the apostle’s pre-selection of “the entire church,” seals of faith, transmigration as purification, and practical piety (fasting/prayer/alms), matching the chapter’s strong pastoral drift and Gardner’s redaction/buddhist-connection flags.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Hagiographic dialogue frame: “Once again…”, “elect stood up”, “apostle”, “I beseech you, my master”.

paragraphs.core_text: ‘Fifteen paths are drawn out in the zone. Four paths are pure and belong [to the] light, leading up to life. Eight other paths are [mixed], leading above from that place. The light shall go [u]p and become free through them; be purified and go in [to the] ships. However, the waste is separated and thrown [dow]n to transmigr[a]tion and the other three paths of [waste ...] discharged to the gehennas’.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the questioner’s introductory frame clause (“For we have heard thus from you:”) while retaining the quoted cosmological schema.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core cosmological-correspondential schematic: numbered structure (15 paths; 4/8/3), impersonal mechanics (Light ascends to ships; Waste separated to transmigration/gehennas) stays within the cosmic system. Embedded via a later Q-summary voice.

paragraphs.core_text: [that the three] paths that belong to waste, the ones that are drawn to the gehennas, [a]re drawn from the fleshes. O[n]e of them is the appetite for [lawl]essness, that of people and of all flesh. The second is the [ ... ] all bodies, which is slaughter, [with] which all flesh is consumed. The third is the damaging action, which [ ... ] the Cross of Light and every body; together with the rest of the error and the blasphemy that wounds the gods.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the reporting attribution (“You have explained…”) as dialogue-frame matter.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic triad defining the three waste-paths with cosmological referents (fleshes, Cross of Light, gehennas) and impersonal definitional tone; the “you have explained” wrapper is later Q&A framing.

paragraphs.core_text: Th[ese th]ree paths [ ... ] lead to the gehennas. And every person shall follow after hi[s] de[e]ds, whether to life or indeed to death.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed second-person instructional attributions (“have you taught us…”, “you have also [told] us…”) while retaining the underlying doctrinal statements.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Concluding axiom linking paths to post-mortem outcome (“follow after his deeds”) functions as part of the cosmological-judgment mechanism; embedded in a later address-to-teacher recap.

Extended question with strong Q-formula (“Now, I beseech you, my master…”) and institutional category “catechumen/faith of God”; functions as editorial dialogue scaffolding for later soteriological discussion.
Continues the disciple’s problem-setting about “catechume/ns… set in the world” before receiving faith; institutional framing rather than impersonal cosmological exposition.
Dialogue attribution (“Then the apostle speaks…”) plus reassurance; classic Kephalaia frame marker (‘apostle’).

Flagged editorial seam: institutional extension about “souls of the elect and the catechumens,” “entire church,” and the apostle’s pre-manifestation selection; cosmos→church mapping and ‘apostle in flesh’ biography signal later institutional theology.
Applies salvation mechanics to contemporary religious landscape (“sects… heresies”) and institutional ‘seal of the faith/knowledge’; angels as pastoral assurance that deeds won’t go to gehennas.
Didactic analogy (royal horse/king’s seal) in service of the catechumen ‘mark of faith’ doctrine; not impersonal cosmic mapping.
Institutional soteriology: catechumen ‘mark/seal of truth,’ ‘form chosen,’ pity, deeds not going to gehennas because of faith; oriented to community identity and assurance.
Explicit church practice layer: fasting, prayer, alms “to the saints,” nullifying earlier deeds; disciplinary/pastoral register dominates.

Institutional rites and ranks (“right hand of peace,” “rank… catechumenate”) integrated with salvation logistics (ship of the night, deeds freed). The overall paragraph is an applied ecclesial soteriology rather than standalone substrate exposition.
Directly asserts catechumen agency to ‘free all his deeds… while being in his body’; pastoral reassurance addressed to catechumen status.
Extended illustrative simile about king/city/host; pedagogical analogy used for applied doctrine rather than systematic cosmological mapping.
Continuation of analogy (some go before/with/after); rhetorical exposition in support of applied soteriology.
Summative reiteration of the analogy; didactic/pastoral style.

Application explicitly to “the catechumen… with his deeds,” using cosmological locations (firmaments, land of the living) but subordinated to institutional catechumen doctrine; not a cosmos→cosmos mapping unit independent of church categories.
Closing instructional reassurance (“I have instructed you…”) about catechumen and angels; pastoral wrap-up rather than core substrate.
